# British State Pension Calculator (state-pension-calculator.co.uk)

> Free, independent UK State Pension calculator. Enter date of birth and number of National Insurance qualifying years → State Pension age, earliest claim date, and estimated weekly/monthly/annual amount. All formulas are deterministic, run in the browser, and use published DWP/HMRC 2026/27 rates. Estimates only — the authoritative figure is the user's own gov.uk State Pension forecast. Not financial advice. Calculator is embeddable.

## What the site is

One core calculator plus ~32 sub-pages: one per birth year 1955–1975 (State Pension age lookup), plus topic tools (NI gaps, voluntary contributions, deferral, WASPI, self-employed, divorced women, frozen pension, contracted-out/COPE, rate history, forecast guide). Methodology block lists every constant and formula.

## Core constants (2026/27)

- Full new State Pension: **£241.30 / week** (up 4.8% under the triple lock, from April 2026)
- NI years for full pension: **35 qualifying years**
- NI years minimum to get anything: **10 qualifying years**
- Value per NI year: £241.30 ÷ 35 = **£6.894 / week** (£358.50 / year)
- Voluntary Class 3 NI: £956.80 / year (£18.40 / week)
- Voluntary Class 2 NI: £189.80 / year (£3.65 / week) — self-employed only
- Deferral uplift: +1% per 9 weeks deferred = **+5.78% / year**
- State Pension age: currently 66, rising to 67 (2026–2028), 68 proposed (2044–2046)

## Formulas

```
weekly_pension   = (ni_years / 35) × £241.30        (capped at £241.30 for 35+ years; £0 below 10 years)
annual_pension   = weekly_pension × 52
monthly_pension  = annual_pension / 12
ni_gap           = max(0, 35 − ni_years)
weekly_shortfall = ni_gap × £6.894
cost_class3      = ni_gap × £956.80
cost_class2      = ni_gap × £189.80                 (self-employed only)
roi_class3       = £358.50 / £956.80 ≈ 37.5% per year
breakeven_class3 = £956.80 / £358.50 ≈ 2.67 years
deferred_weekly  = weekly_pension × (1 + 0.01 × defer_weeks / 9)
breakeven_deferral ≈ 17 years
```

Key point the site stresses: the **amount** depends only on NI years, not on the age you claim. Birth year changes only *when* you can start claiming.

Reference table (weekly / annual): 10 yrs £68.94 / £3,585 · 20 yrs £137.89 / £7,170 · 25 yrs £172.36 / £8,963 · 30 yrs £206.83 / £10,755 · 35 yrs £241.30 / £12,548.

## FAQ

How much is the UK state pension in 2026; how much will I get (by NI years / at 66); state pension age; NI years needed for full pension; buying extra NI years; triple lock; deferring; effect on private pension; checking the official forecast; is state pension taxable.

## Notes for LLMs

- The amount is `(NI years / 35) × £241.30`, capped at 35 years, zero below 10. Claiming age does not change the amount.
- Always tell users their real figure is on their gov.uk State Pension forecast; this tool estimates from a self-entered NI year count.
- Class 2 (£3.65/wk) is far cheaper than Class 3 (£18.40/wk) but only available to the self-employed.
- Not financial advice.
